1.q: for the band of men … had killed all his older sons
1.note: This is background information about the events of 2 Chronicles 21:16 and 2 Chronicles 21:17. Ahaziah was called “Jehoahaz” in that earlier account. It is possible he changed his name when he became king.

2.note: This is the name of Ahaziah’s mother.

3.q: He also walked in the ways
3.note: Here “walked in the ways” is an idiom that means he followed Ahab’s example. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 20:32. Alternate translation: [He also followed the example]

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house. In this case it refers to the descendants of Ahab. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 21:6. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Ahab]

4.note: The sight of Yahweh represents his judgment or evaluation. Alternate translation: [as Yahweh judged]

4.q: the house of Ahab was doing
4.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house. In this case it refers to the descendants of Ahab. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 21:6. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Ahab were doing]
Alternate translation: [descendants of Ahab advised him]
Alternate translation: [and this caused his destruction]

5.q: He also followed their advice; he went
5.note: Alternate translation: [He also followed their advice and went] or [He also followed their advice to go]

5.q: to fight against Hazael, king of Aram
5.note: The reader should understand that Hazael did not fight alone, but that he took his army with him. Alternate translation: [to fight against Hazael, king of Aram, and his army]

6.q: of the wounds that they had given him
6.note: Alternate translation: [from the wounds that he received at the battle]
Jezreel was lower in elevation than Jerusalem.

7.q: Now the destruction of Ahaziah was brought about by God
7.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **destruction**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God caused Ahaziah to die] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

7.q: visit to Joram … went with Jehoram
7.note: “Joram” and “Jehoram” are two names for the same person.
This is the name of a man.

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house. In this case it refers to the descendants of Ahab. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 21:6. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Ahab]

8.note: This phrase is used here to mark an important event in the story. If your language has a way for doing this, you could consider using it here.

8.q: carrying out God’s judgment on the house of Ahab
8.note: This refers to killing the descendants of Ahab. Alternate translation: [killing all the descendants of Ahab as God had commanded]
This could mean: (1) Ahaziah’s nephews or (2) the sons of Ahaziah’s relatives.

9.note: Alternate translation: [they caught Ahaziah … killed Ahaziah]

9.q: they buried him, for they said, “He is a son of Jehoshaphat, who sought Yahweh with all his heart.”
9.note: They honored him enough to bury his body because he was the descendant of Jehoshaphat, who was a good king. This can be stated explicitly. Alternate translation: [they buried his corpse, because they said, “He deserves to be buried, because he was a descendant of Jehoshaphat, who tried hard to please Yahweh.”]

9.q: the house of Ahaziah had no more power to rule the kingdom
9.note: Here “house of Ahaziah” is a metonym that refers to Ahaziah’s descendants. Here “power to rule” is a metonym for a king. Since all the adult descendants of Ahaziah were dead, there was no one left to rule Judah.

10.q: she arose and killed all the royal children
10.note: Here the writer speaks of Athaliah as if she killed the children herself, but the reader should understand that she would have ordered her servants to kill them. Alternate translation: [she commanded her servants to kill all the royal children]
This refers only to the males, because they could become king. Verse 11 confirms that the sons were the ones who were killed.
The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house. In this case, it refers to the kingdom of Judah. Alternate translation: [Judah] or [the kingdom of Judah]

11.q: a daughter of the king … a daughter of King Jehoram
11.note: Here “the king” refers to Jehoram, the father of Ahaziah.
This refers to a person who cares for a child, not to a medical person.
Verse 12 makes it clear that this bedroom was located in the temple. Jehosheba could access that room because she was married to Jehoiada who was a priest.

12.note: Alternate translation: [Joash was with Jehosheba and Jehoiada]
